claim: Let \(X,Y\) be jointly distributed integrable real random variables, and interpret the two weighted conditional terms in Ghosh and Nanda's conditional \(\mathcal L_1\) precedence definition by their equivalent truncated expectations. Then the relation is exactly the mean order, with no independence assumption: \(X\le_{\mathrm{cp-}\mathcal L_1}Y\) if and only if \(\mathbb E X\le\mathbb E Y\). Indeed, if \(A=\mathbb E[(Y-X)\mathbf 1_{\{X<Y\}}]\) and \(B=\mathbb E[(X-Y)\mathbf 1_{\{X>Y\}}]\), then the defining comparison is \(A\ge B\) and \(A-B=\mathbb E(Y-X)\). Consequently the relation is invariant under every change of dependence that preserves the two marginal means, and equality in both directions holds exactly when the means are equal.
integrity: The proof is a direct integrable positive-part identity valid for arbitrary joint laws. No numerical experiment, asymptotic approximation, independence assumption, or external certificate is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns only the conditional L1 precedence relation of the cited source. It does not apply to the source's nonlinear conditional K* precedence order or to other stochastic orders. Literature searches cannot exclude an unpublished or unindexed prior observation.
title: Conditional L1 precedence is exactly mean order under arbitrary dependence
